findings.message: The source guard scans a broader statement than the consumed path operand: classify_line matches the tokens 'request' and 'path' anywhere in the raw line text, so the assignment target manufactures the untrusted-path signal. Counterexample: classify_line("request_cache_path = os.path.join(BASE, 'static')") returns 'untrusted-path' because the trigger sits in the left-hand side of the assignment, and classify_line('# handles the request path') returns 'untrusted-path' from a comment mentioning the request path; the invented assignment cache_label = 'request path' classifies the same way with no untrusted operand. Moving the tokens to an irrelevant syntactic position flips the classification with no untrusted data, so the source-detection boundary the tests pin is raw statement text, not the operand; the positive test passes for the wrong reason. Classify the consumed operand (the RHS after the assignment separator, comments stripped) instead of the statement text.
